assumptions: Iu = 250 A is taken as the frame rating and In = 250 A as the sensor/rating-plug value, so frame/sensor/plug are all reported as 250 A.

Trip unit 'Ekip DIP LI' is an electronic (static) unit, so has_trip_unit=true and trip_type_id=1 (Static Trip); LI means long-time + instantaneous only, and with no Ig/tg dials or GF test button on the plate the breaker is treated as having no ground-fault function.
UL 1066 / ANSI Cat. B construction places this in the Low-Voltage Power Circuit Breaker subtype rather than a molded-case subtype.

Applicable interrupting voltage: the plate states Icu at 480 V directly, matching the asset's existing 480V voltage attribute, so the 100 kA figure is the governing rating (operating_voltage in context was null).

Ampere Rating custom attribute left blank because its options stop at 150A and the true rating is 250A; Voltage attribute left at its existing '480V' value (not overwritten); Catalog Number left blank because the plate prints only a type designation and a serial, no separate catalog number.
The 'Breaker Settings' attribute was left blank because the trip-unit dip-switch face is not in the photo set.

agent.reasoning: The nameplate clearly reads ABB SACE Emax 2, Type E1.2 N 250, Ekip DIP LI, In=Iu=250A, 3P, 480 V AC, Icu=Ics=100 kA @ 480 V, UL 1066. SKM does model this family — the Ekip DIP 'LI' variant (cdevice_oid 318402) even has a 250 A frame with a 250 A sensor and 250 A plug — but I checked the complete frame trees of every E1.2 entry (DIP LI, DIP LSI, Touch, Hi-Touch) and they only offer 42, 50 and 65 kA at 254/508/635 V; the applicable 250 A/508 V frame for this 480 V asset is 65 kA. Since no E1.2 frame provides the plate's 100 kA, and the one 100 kA/250 A/508 V frame in the library belongs to the physically different E2.2 breaker, every candidate contradicts the nameplate on interrupting class, which is part of the device's identity and not a warnable approximation. I therefore left skm_oid/skm_settings off, kept ABB and all nameplate-derived fields including nameplate_interrupt_ka=100, and spelled out the contradiction (likely an E1.2 H rather than N) plus the un-photographed Ekip DIP switch banks for human follow-up.

warnings: No SKM match: plate reads ABB SACE Emax 2, Type E1.2 N 250, Ekip DIP LI, In=Iu=250A, 3P, Ue=480V AC, Icu=Ics=100 kA @ 480 V, Cat B, UL 1066. Searched ABB (canonical id 3), SACE (id 108, empty) and queries 'Emax 2', 'Emax', 'E1.2', 'Ekip' across mccb-/pcb-/iccb-breakers; the only E1.2 entries are 318402 (Ekip DIP LI), 318448 (DIP LSI), 318598/318646 (Touch), 318498 (Hi-Touch) plus their GF companions. Frame trees of all E1.2 entries were inspected: every frame at 254/508/635 V offers only 42, 50 or 65 kA — the applicable 250 A/508 V frame is 65 kA, so no E1.2 frame anywhere provides the plate's 100 kA. The E2.2 entry does have a 250 A/508 V/100 kA frame, but E2.2 is a different, larger frame than the plate's E1.2, so binding it would contradict the nameplate type. Also note the plate is internally inconsistent with ABB published data: E1.2 'N' is the 65/66 kA class and 100 kA @ 480 V is the E1.2 'H' class — verify in the field whether this is an E1.2 H (or an E2.2) before designating.

Trip settings not captured: the Ekip DIP unit is adjustable (I1/t1/I3 dip-switch banks) but only the rating nameplate was photographed, so no switch positions could be read — actual field settings are unknown.
